title: Speed Switches
eyebrow: Friction audit and design for approval · nothing built yet

short.lead: A Fable 5.2 session spent half your usage on design steps before any code was written. The audit below found why. Switches already exist, but they are environment settings in settings.json that need a restart, and switching the design loop off removes only the hooks. The rule text that tells the model to make pages, wait for approvals and send work to builder helpers is still injected every session, so the model keeps doing the ceremony anyway. This design adds two switches you type in chat, makes them remove the rule text as well as the hooks, and fixes the foreground waits and the two-run test limit.
short.hint: Tap a part to see what changes and what it needs from you.
items: You type "design loop off" and the next reply just does the work
No design page, no approval lock, no issues-before-code and no editor pass. The safety guards stay on: no destructive commands, no commits on main, success claims still need a run behind them.
You type the line once; it holds for this repo until you type "design loop on".
"builders off" keeps the work in the main conversation
The delegation rule stops being injected and its hooks stop counting, so artistic work is done by the model you chose instead of a cheaper helper that falls short.
A foreground wait loop is refused before it runs

The command in your screenshot, a 10-minute `until grep ...; do sleep 20; done` wrapped in `timeout 595 bash -c`, is refused with a pointer to run_in_background, which wakes the model when the task ends instead of holding the turn.
Reruns are counted against changes, not commits

Today a test script may run twice, then is refused until a new code commit. After this, the count resets whenever any file changes, and only a third run of the same command on unchanged files is refused.

changes: keep
What exists today: six switches, all in settings.json

HOUSE_RULES_LOOP, HOUSE_RULES_ISSUES, HOUSE_RULES_DELEGATION, HOUSE_RULES_AGENTS, HOUSE_RULES_EDITOR and HOUSE_RULES_RERUNS are read from the env block of settings.json. Changing one means editing that file by hand and starting a new session. These stay as the long-term default; the typed switches sit on top.
list
Read in scripts/house_rules/design_loop.py (_loop_enabled, line 2536), delegation.py (lines 165 and 877) and safe_git.py (line 548).
cross
Friction 1: the off switch leaves the rules text in place

With HOUSE_RULES_LOOP=off the hooks stop, but event_showrule in scripts/house_rules/core.py (line 620) still injects show-dont-tell.md, the rule that says every plan is a page and every session starts locked. The model obeys the text, so the tokens are spent anyway.
list

Fix: when a switch is off, its rule section is left out of the injected text and a one-line note says which switch removed it, the same way HOUSE_RULES_VOICE=off already removes the voice section (core.py line 454).
cross
Friction 2: three approval pages per change

A change goes design page, then build plan page with drawn pictures of the planned code, then QA page. Each page also goes past the editor helper. Phase 1 (#493) produced a design page and a build plan page before any code. For a capable model and a clear request this is where most of the usage goes.
list
Light mode skips the design and build plan pages. The QA page stays optional: offered, not required.
cross
Friction 3: six end-of-reply checks that each force another turn

The checkpoint table in design_loop.py (line 2143) runs page, editor, evidence, commit, handoff, plain summary and QA page checks. Six of the seven block, and every block makes the model write the reply again, which costs a whole extra turn.
list
Light mode keeps evidence and commit (they protect your work) and drops editor, handoff, plain summary and QA page.
cross
Friction 4: delegation is mandatory past one file or three steps

The rule in house-rules.md (line 118) sends every settled plan to builder helpers, one per issue, at most two at a time, each in its own worktree. Each helper starts cold and rereads what the main conversation already knew. For art, layout and feel, helpers fall short and the work is redone.
list
"builders off" removes that rule section and turns off HOUSE_RULES_DELEGATION and HOUSE_RULES_AGENTS checks for the repo.
cross
Friction 5: a plan over three steps needs GitHub issues before any code
The issue gate refuses source edits until a parent issue and one child per step exist, each labelled. That is several GitHub calls and a written issue body per step before work starts.
list
Light mode turns this gate off too (it is the HOUSE_RULES_ISSUES switch today).
cross
Friction 6: foreground waits are not caught
Nothing in the guard looks at sleep loops. Claude Code refuses a bare foreground sleep, but wrapping it in bash -c with timeout gets through, and the turn sits blocked for up to ten minutes.
list
A new guard pattern in scripts/house_rules/safe_git.py refuses a foreground Bash command that loops with sleep, or uses timeout over 60 seconds, unless run_in_background is set.
cross
Friction 7: two runs per test script per commit

RERUN_LIMIT = 2 in safe_git.py (line 533) counts runs since the last code commit. A flaky test, a suite run with different filters, or the rule's own "run what you touched twice" uses both runs, and the third is refused even after files were fixed but not yet committed.
list
The count is keyed on the command plus a hash of the working tree. Any file change resets it; a third identical run on identical files is refused.
new
One fix carried in from #515

Phase 1 step 8 (#515) found that with the loop off, the close guard still demands QA evidence only the loop can record. The switch design here covers it: every guard fed by a switched-off part is off with it.
list
#515 stays the issue for that part; this design decides its open question.
choices: q1
How do you flip the switches?
A
Type a line in chat: "design loop off", "builders off" (and "on"), saved for this repo; /house-rules:mode does the same and shows the current state
Works in the desktop app, on your phone and in cloud sessions, takes effect on the next message, needs no restart. It is how approvals already work.
B
A slash command only: /house-rules:mode light or full
One clear place, but it is unavailable where slash commands are not, and still writes the same state file.
C
Keep settings.json only, and just make it remove the rule text
Smallest change, but still a hand edit and a restart for each flip.
A matches how you already approve things and needs nothing outside the chat.
q2
What is the starting state for a repo nobody has switched?
A
Chosen by model: light for Opus and Fable, full for Sonnet and Haiku; your typed switch always wins
The session start hook already sees the model name, and it matches your point that the full loop suits smaller models.
B
Always full until you switch it
Predictable, but every frontier session pays the cost until you remember to switch.
A puts the default where you said it belongs and keeps the override one line away.
q3
What does "design loop off" turn off?
A

Design and build plan pages, the approval lock, issues-before-code, the editor pass, the 160-word page rule, and the handoff, plain summary and QA page checks. Kept: destructive-command guard, main-branch guard, evidence and commit checks
Removes the ceremony and keeps everything that protects your files and your history.
B
All of the above, plus the evidence and commit checks
Cheapest, but a success claim with no run behind it would go through unchallenged.
A keeps the two checks that have caught real mistakes.
q4
How strict is the test rerun check?
A
Reset on any file change; refuse the third identical run on unchanged files
Stops the edit-nothing-and-retry loop it was built for, without blocking real fix-and-rerun cycles.
B
Keep counting since the last commit, but raise the limit to five
One-line change, but the friction comes back on longer debugging.
C
Off by default, on only in full mode
No friction, but loses the guard for frontier models too.
A targets the thrashing the check exists for and leaves real work alone.
q5
What happens to a long foreground wait?
A
Refused, with the run_in_background form of the same command in the refusal
The turn is never held, and the model has the fix in hand.
B
Allowed, with a note afterwards
Softer, but the ten minutes are already spent when the note arrives.
A prevents the wait instead of reporting it.

wrapup.summary: An audit of the house-rules design loop found seven points of friction. This design adds two typed switches (design loop and builders) that remove both the hooks and the rule text, a guard against foreground waits, and a rerun check that counts changes instead of commits.
